draft.goal:
A small Python word-counting CLI called tally counts words in explicitly named text files and prints predictable per-file counts, for local users.
Why: Keep the scope small and make the behavior easy to test.
Must: be written in Python.
Must: count words in explicitly named text files.
Must: print per-file counts.
options: Minimal command-line interface — benefit: Keeps the scope small and behavior easy to test.; cost: Provides only the explicitly requested counting behavior.; undo cost: Low; additional options can be added later.

nodes.answer: Most likely failure: tally mutates source files or has surprising counting/output behavior. Settled choices: tally is strictly read-only: never modify, create, or delete input files or other repository files at runtime. Use Python 3 standard library only. Accept one or more explicit UTF-8 text file paths; stdin is out of scope. Refuse directories with a plain stderr error. Words are whitespace-separated tokens using str.split(). Print exactly '<count> <path>' per file in argument order, with no total. No arguments or unreadable/invalid UTF-8 files produce a plain stderr error and exit 1; success exits 0. Tests use unittest with temporary files and verify counts, output, errors, and unchanged input bytes. No packaging or recursive traversal.
